threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the buskers in the Square. A true Hackneyer knows they’re just part of the scenery now.
Last night, the 133 was a circus. A guy in a clown costume kept juggling, while two others argued over the last slice of pizza. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a man at the bus stop teaching his parrot to swear in German, I realized Neukölln was home. It's those little moments that stick with you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bar where the cocktails are served in mismatched teacups. It's like sipping a classic with a side of chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their reaction to BART delays; they just shrug and keep scrolling their phone, while the newbies panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy playing the sax on the 31 just past Market. Reminded me why we endure the delays—moments of pure San Francisco magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just another stop for tapas, but it’s the locals’ hidden corners, like Carrer de Mozart, that tell the real story.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their stunned look at the metro map—perplexed by the bizarre lines but still trying to sound casual about taking the L1 instead of the L2.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'thank you' to the bus driver. The locals just nod, like it's a covert sign of respect in the game of commuting.
Last night on the 59, a guy argued with his imaginary friend about the best chicken shop in Brixton. Only in South London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was part of Neukölln was when I heard two kids arguing over who could jump higher off the local playground swings—not a care in the world.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a currywurst stand sharing space with an artisanal cheese shop. Street food meets gourmet, and the lines tell you it's an experience.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: True locals know to avoid BART after 8pm on game nights. The way tourists cram in, it’s like watching a game without knowing the rules.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 last night, the driver yelled 'Keep your dogs off the seats, folks!' just as a guy with a chihuahua sat down. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the ‘Gràcia vibe’ is all about the plazas, but it’s really about the street corners where locals just nod and share a quiet moment.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they’re new when they still call it 'Barcelona' instead of 'Barna' and look confused at the late dinner hours.
